When you're in the thick of the action—whether you're battling a dangerous foe, evading a trap, or racing against the clock—youʼll be operating in whatʼs called Action Economy. This mode breaks time into 5-second intervals, where every moment counts. Each characterʼs actions must be completed within this short timeframe, meaning players need to make quick, tactical decisions. During Action Economy, you'll focus on: •Specific Actions: Whether it's attacking, dodging, using abilities, or interacting with the environment, youʼre acting fast and efficiently to achieve your goal.

Outside of high-intensity moments, the game transitions into Downtime Play, where the pace slows down and the focus shifts to long-term decisions and character growth. Instead of focusing on immediate actions, Downtime allows your character to step back, engage in personal development, and interact with the world in more meaningful ways. During Downtime, youʼll focus on: •Character Development: Training, learning new abilities, or improving existing ones. •Exploration and Interaction: Engaging in deep social interactions, crafting, exploring, or pursuing personal goals. •Long-Term Planning: Instead of solving problems in the moment, youʼre setting up strategies and working toward bigger, more personal objectives that will unfold over time. Downtime Play gives you the chance to explore your characterʼs deeper motivations and influences, take on projects that require extended effort, and enrich your roleplaying experience. It's where your character truly grows and prepares for the challenges that await.
Participants must adhere to strict rules during MRC events to ensure fairness and safety:

1.Planeswalkersʼ Link: •Mechanics: This magical ability allows the user to send limited telepathic or visual messages across dimensions. Requires a magical artifact to focus. •Message Limit: 10 words per message, with a cooldown period of 8 hours. •Casting Requirements: DC 18 Arcana or Willpower check. If failed, the link collapses and causes 1d6 psychic damage to the user. •Interference and Range: Messaging accuracy decreases if crossing more than one dimension. For each additional layer, the targetʼs Willpower check (DC 12) must succeed to receive the message accurately. •Artifacts: Rare items (such as Planar Amulets) are needed to channel the Link, often sought after by high-level mages. 2.Soul Echoes:

◦ Ritual requires 30 minutes and a DC 15 Ritual or Arcana check. ◦ The soul-bound message can last up to 48 hours before it fades, or until delivered. •Risks: Using Soul Echoes creates a temporary psychic link between caster and receiver, leaving both vulnerable to mind-linking entities. •Interference: Certain high-arcana zones may cause message distortion or attract unwanted entities to the echo. •Message Limit: Only one Soul Echo message can be active per caster at any time. 3.Ethereal Messengers: •Mechanics: These are magical constructs or spirits bound to carry a message across dimensions. •Message Limit: Can carry longer messages or small items, though items must be non-metallic and weigh less than 1 lb. •Construct Ritual: Requires 15 minutes of spellcasting and 1d4 magical reagents. Success depends on a DC 14 Magic check. •Distortion and Risks: With each dimension, the messenger absorbs surrounding energies, adding a 10% chance of message distortion. If distortion occurs, the message may garble or convey unintended words. •Life Span: Messengers exist only for 24 hours or until they deliver their message.

◦ Each message sent has a 30% chance to pull energy from chaotic beings, drawing them to the casterʼs location. ◦ Receivers must make an Insight or Perception check (DC 15) to comprehend the message due to its unpredictable frequency. •Usage Limit: Once per day, as prolonged usage attracts reality-warping entities. 2.Bound Entities: •

1.Establishing Connection: •Setup: Ansible connections require 1 action to initiate contact and must synchronize across dimensions. The synchronization process takes 5 rounds (or 30 seconds in real-time). •Skill Check: Roll a Technology or Arcana check (DC 18). On a failure, the Ansible cannot connect, and 1 Ether Core or power equivalent is lost. Critical failures may temporarily deactivate the Ansible, requiring repairs. •Connection Confirmation: Once connected, both users can communicate in real-time, with negligible delay. The connection remains open until power is cut or interrupted. 2.Message Security: •Encryption: Ansibles utilize high-level encryption; interception is possible but requires a high- level decryption attempt. •Decryption Difficulty: Intercepting a message requires a DC 25 Decryption check. Messages not decrypted within 1 minute (10 rounds) will self-scramble. •Additional Safeguards: Advanced users may add magical sigils or warding spells, adding a +2 DC to any interception attempt. 3.Maintenance and Reliability: •Regular Maintenance: The Ansible system must be checked regularly. Every 10 hours of continuous use, an Engineering or Magic Maintenance check (DC 15) is required to ensure stable operation. •Overload and Instability: Prolonged use without breaks may cause an Ansible to overheat. After 8 hours, each additional hour requires a DC 18 Maintenance check; failure results in a temporary shutdown for 1d4 hours. •Cross-Dimensional Interference: Ansibles are susceptible to interference in high-energy or unstable dimensions. In chaotic or magic-saturated realities, any message has a 10% chance of mild distortion. 4.Risks of Disruptions: •Anomaly Creation: If an Ansible is damaged during an active connection, an anomaly may form (10% chance). This can result in echoes (repeating messages) or “ghost signals” (unintended information leaks). •Dimensional Spillover: If the Ansible becomes unstable while connecting dimensions, a spillover of energy may occur, potentially leaking reality fragments or altering the immediate areaʼs properties for a short time. 5.Cost and Availability: •Access Fees: Each use of an Ansible requires either financial cost (often controlled by factions or governments) or rare resources like Ether Cores.

•Anchors are often tied to constants (death, destruction, invention). •Mutable Nodes usually have variables tied to character choice or randomness. •Changing a Mutable Node may convert it into a new Anchor in a divergent timeline. GMs should designate nodes during prep or dynamically in-session, using fate currents and character impact to determine what “must” happen and what can happen.

•When a player creates a branch, the GM may: ◦ Log the new timeline under a Reality Code. ◦ Apply Desync Penalties when returning to older timelines. ◦ Introduce Echo Fallout, where NPCs remember different versions of events. Optional Rule – Divergence Resonance: The further a character travels from their native timelineʼs sequence, the more likely they are to suffer emotional, mental, or physical dissonance. These can manifest as hallucinations, phantom injuries, or fate storms.
“The laws may change, the gods may lie, the sky may melt—but wherever thereʼs people, thereʼs politics.”
Players can attempt to consolidate fractured memories with a Willpower or Sanity Check (DC 18). On failure, gain a Trigger, flaw, or hallucination related to the timeline breach.
When using non-native languages in high-context situations, the GM may call for an Insight or Persuasion check (DC 12–20) to avoid misunderstanding, insult, or distortion.

•Multiversal deja vu Over time, multiple selves may converge, pulling knowledge or traits from their counterparts. This is known as Echo Convergence and can occur: •Through advanced magic or rituals. •When exposed to a Nexus or Fate Current intersection. •As a result of timeline collapse or forced assimilation.

When encountering a potential Echo Self, players may attempt a Recognition Check to determine the degree of resonance. Recognition Check = Willpower + Sanity Modifier + 1d20 •DC varies based on level of divergence, distance between realities, and syncing status. •A success allows the character to intuit shared memories, thoughts, or feelings.

When engaging in diplomatic or political interaction in a new reality, players may roll: History or Diplomacy check (DC 14–20) Success allows them to avoid faux pas based on incorrect historical assumptions.

Effect: Bind a curse to a fetish doll. •As long as you possess the doll and a connection to the target, you may deal 1d4 psychic damage per round (no action required). •Lasts up to 10 rounds or 10 minutes. •Backlash: If the doll is destroyed or lost, take 1d6 psychic damage and roll vs corruption.

To enter a trance, the practitioner must: •Spend 10 minutes preparing (meditating, using ritual tools, etc.). •Roll a Wisdom or Constitution saving throw (DC 15). Success: The practitioner enters an altered state and remains connected to the spirit world for 1d4 hours. Failure: The connection fails. If failed by 5 or more, the practitioner gains 1 level of exhaustion.

At the end of the trance or when ending it prematurely, the practitioner rolls a DC 12 Constitution check: Success: Exit the state safely. Failure: Gain 1 level of exhaustion from spiritual fatigue. Use of grounding herbs or talismans can reduce or remove this penalty.

To communicate with a spirit: •Make a Wisdom check: ◦ DC 10 for minor spirits (animals, elementals, local echoes) ◦ DC 15 for greater spirits (totem lords, ancestors, guardian entities) Offerings or respected behavior can reduce the DC by 2–5. On success, the spirit communicates via emotions, impressions, visions, or words. On failure, the spirit may ignore the practitioner—or, if offended, react negatively.

Practitioners may engage in brief meditations to reconnect between trances. Once per long rest, they may: •Spend 10 minutes meditating with a spirit or totem. •Roll Wisdom (DC 10) to receive a spiritual insight, cryptic vision, or hint related to a current goal. If performed in a sacred place or near a spirit, they may reroll the check or gain advantage.
